title.zh: 卷一百九十下 列傳第一百四十下: 文苑下
title.raw: 卷一百九十下 列傳第一百四十下: 文苑下 Volume 190 Biographies 140: Men of Letters 3

sentences.zh: 李華字遐叔，趙郡人。

translations.literal: Li Hua, style name Xiashu, was a man of Zhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hua, whose courtesy name was Xiashu, came from Zhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 開元二十三年進士擢第。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Kaiyuan he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In 735 he passed the jinshi civil examination.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，登朝為監察御史。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era he entered court as a supervisory censor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao reign he entered court service as a supervisory censor.

sentences.zh: 累轉侍御史，禮部、吏部二員外郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted in turn to attendant censor and to vice director in the Ministries of Rites and Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in turn to attendant censor and to vice director in both the Ministry of Rites and the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 華善屬文，與蘭陵蕭穎士友善。

translations.literal: Hua was skilled at literary composition and was friendly with Xiao Yingshi of Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: Hua excelled at literary composition and was on friendly terms with Xiao Yingshi of Lanling.

sentences.zh: 華進士時，著含元殿賦萬餘言，穎士見而賞之，曰：「景福之上，靈光之下。

translations.literal: When Hua was a jinshi candidate he wrote a Rhapsody on the Hanyuan Hall of more than ten thousand characters; Yingshi read it and praised it, saying: "Above the Jingfu, below the Lingguang."
translations.idiomatic: While still a jinshi candidate, Hua composed a Rhapsody on the Hanyuan Hall of more than ten thousand characters. Yingshi read it and exclaimed, "It ranks above the Jingfu and below the Lingguang."

sentences.zh: 」華文體溫麗，少宏傑之氣，穎士詞鋒俊發，華自以所業過之，疑其誣詞。

translations.literal: Hua's style was warm and elegant, with little grand and heroic spirit; Yingshi's phrasing was sharp and brilliant. Hua believed his own work surpassed Yingshi's and suspected his praise was false.
translations.idiomatic: Hua wrote in a warm, elegant style with little of the grand and heroic, whereas Yingshi's diction was sharp and brilliant. Hua thought his own work the better and suspected that Yingshi's praise was insincere.

sentences.zh: 乃為祭古戰場文，熏汙之如故物，置於佛書之閣。

translations.literal: He therefore wrote his Lament for an Ancient Battlefield, smoked and stained it to look like an old object, and placed it in a Buddhist scripture repository.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore composed his Lament for an Ancient Battlefield, smoked and smudged the manuscript until it looked like an old relic, and hid it among Buddhist texts.

sentences.zh: 華與穎士因閱佛書得之，華謂之曰：「此文何如？

translations.literal: While Hua and Yingshi were browsing Buddhist books they found it; Hua said to him: "How is this piece?"
translations.idiomatic: While Hua and Yingshi were leafing through Buddhist books they came upon it. Hua asked him, "How do you rate this essay?"

sentences.zh: 」穎士曰：「可矣。

translations.literal: Yingshi said: "It will do."
translations.idiomatic: Yingshi replied, "It will do."

sentences.zh: 」華曰：「當代秉筆者，誰及於此？

translations.literal: Hua said: "Among those who wield the brush in our age, who could equal this?"
translations.idiomatic: Hua asked, "Among the leading writers of our day, who could match this?"

sentences.zh: 」穎士曰：「君稍精思，便可及此。

translations.literal: Yingshi said: "If you refine your thinking a little, you could reach this level yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Yingshi answered, "If you give the matter a little more thought, you could write at this level yourself."

sentences.zh: 」華愕然。

translations.literal: Hua was stunned.
translations.idiomatic: Hua was dumbfounded.

sentences.zh: 華著論言龜卜可廢，通人當其言。

translations.literal: Hua wrote a treatise arguing that tortoise and milfoil divination should be abolished; men of insight agreed with his view.
translations.idiomatic: Hua wrote a treatise arguing that tortoise-shell and milfoil divination ought to be abandoned, and thoughtful men endorsed his position.

sentences.zh: 祿山陷京師，玄宗出幸，華扈從不及，陷賊，偽署為鳳閣舍人。

translations.literal: When Lushan took the capital, Emperor Xuanzong fled on tour; Hua could not keep up with the entourage, was trapped by the rebels, and was given a false appointment as Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan seized the capital, Emperor Xuanzong fled the court. Hua failed to join the imperial entourage, fell into rebel hands, and was given a false appointment as Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 收城後，三司類例減等，從輕貶官，遂廢於家，卒。

translations.literal: After the city was recovered, under the Three Offices' categories his case was reduced by one grade; he was demoted on the lenient scale, was dismissed to live at home, and died.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital was retaken, the Three Offices classified his offense at a reduced grade and demoted him leniently. He was then dismissed to live at home, where he died.

sentences.zh: 華嘗為魯山令元德秀墓碑，顏真卿書，李陽冰篆額，後人爭模寫之，號為「四絕碑」。

translations.literal: Hua once composed the epitaph for Magistrate Yuan Dexiu of Lushan; Yan Zhenqing wrote the text, Li Yangbing carved the title in seal script; later men vied to copy it, and it was called the Stele of Four Excellences.
translations.idiomatic: Hua once wrote the epitaph for Yuan Dexiu, magistrate of Lushan; Yan Zhenqing penned the inscription and Li Yangbing cut the title in seal script. Later generations copied it eagerly, and it became known as the "Stele of Four Excellences."

sentences.zh: 有文集十卷，行於時。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in ten juan circulating in his time.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works in ten juan circulated widely in his day.

sentences.zh: 李商隐，字义山，怀州河内人。

translations.literal: Li Shangyin, style name Yishan, was a man of Henei in Huai prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shangyin, whose courtesy name was Yishan, came from Henei in Huai prefecture.

sentences.zh: 曾祖叔恒，年十九登进士第，位终安阳令。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Shuhuan passed the jinshi at nineteen and ended as magistrate of Anyang.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Shuhuan passed the jinshi examination at nineteen and ended his career as magistrate of Anyang.

sentences.zh: 祖俌，位终邢州录事参军。

translations.literal: His grandfather Fu ended as recording secretary of Xing prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Fu rose no higher than recording secretary of Xing prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父嗣。

translations.literal: His father was Si.
translations.idiomatic: His father was Si.

sentences.zh: 商隐幼能为文。

translations.literal: Shangyin could compose essays while still young.
translations.idiomatic: Shangyin could already write essays as a boy.

sentences.zh: 令狐楚镇河阳，以所业文干之，年才及弱冠。

translations.literal: When Linghu Chu was military commissioner of Heyang, Shangyin presented his writings to him; he had not yet reached twenty.
translations.idiomatic: When Linghu Chu governed Heyang as military commissioner, Shangyin presented his writings to him, though he had not yet turned twenty.

sentences.zh: 楚以其少俊，深礼之，令与诸子游。

translations.literal: Chu regarded him as young and talented, treated him with deep courtesy, and had him associate with his sons.
translations.idiomatic: Chu admired his youth and talent, treated him with exceptional courtesy, and let him mingle with his sons.

sentences.zh: 楚镇天平、汴州，从为巡官，岁给资装，令随计上都。

translations.literal: When Chu governed Tianping and Bian prefectures, Shangyin followed him as a staff officer; Chu supplied his travel expenses yearly and sent him to the capital with the tribute mission for the examination.
translations.idiomatic: When Chu served at Tianping and Bian, Shangyin followed him as a staff officer. Chu paid his travel expenses each year and sent him to the capital with the tribute mission to sit for the examination.

sentences.zh: 开成二年，方登进士第，释褐秘书省校书郎，调补弘农尉。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaicheng he finally passed the jinshi, was first appointed proofreader in the Secretariat, and was later transferred to magistrate of Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: In 837 he finally passed the jinshi examination, took his first office as proofreader in the Secretariat, and was later transferred to magistrate of Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 会昌二年，又以书判拔萃。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huichang he again passed the examination for outstanding legal and documentary skill.
translations.idiomatic: In 842 he again distinguished himself in the examination for legal and documentary excellence.

sentences.zh: 王茂元镇河阳，辟为掌书记，得待御史。

translations.literal: When Wang Maoyuan was commissioner of Heyang, he recruited Shangyin as chief clerk and obtained for him the post of awaiting imperial disposition as censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Maoyuan governed Heyang, he recruited Shangyin as chief clerk and secured for him appointment as censor awaiting imperial disposition.

sentences.zh: 茂元爱其才，以子妻之。

translations.literal: Maoyuan admired his talent and gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Maoyuan admired his talent and gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 茂元虽读书为儒，然本将家子，李德裕素遇之，时德裕秉政，用为河阳帅。

translations.literal: Although Maoyuan had studied and was a Confucian scholar, he was by origin from a military family; Li Deyu had long favored him, and at the time Deyu held power and appointed him commander of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Maoyuan had studied the classics and was a Confucian in learning, yet he came from a military family. Li Deyu had long favored him, and while Deyu held power he appointed him commander of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 德裕与李宗闵、杨嗣复、令狐楚大相仇怨。

translations.literal: Deyu bore great enmity toward Li Zongmin, Yang Sifu, and Linghu Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu was locked in bitter enmity with Li Zongmin, Yang Sifu, and Linghu Chu.

sentences.zh: 商隐既为茂元从事，宗闵党大薄之。

translations.literal: Since Shangyin had entered Maoyuan's service, Zongmin's faction looked down on him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shangyin entered Maoyuan's service, Zongmin's faction held him in deep contempt.

sentences.zh: 时令狐楚已卒，子绹为员外郎，以商隐背恩，尤恶其无行。

translations.literal: By then Linghu Chu had died; his son Tao was an outer court official. Regarding Shangyin as ungrateful, he especially detested his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: By then Linghu Chu had died and his son Tao held an outer court post. Tao regarded Shangyin as ungrateful and especially despised his lack of principle.

sentences.zh: 俄而茂元卒，来游京师，久之不调。

translations.literal: Before long Maoyuan died; Shangyin came to the capital seeking office but went long without appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Maoyuan died. Shangyin came to the capital in search of office but remained unemployed for a long time.

sentences.zh: 会给事中郑亚廉察桂州，请为观察判官、检校水部员外郎。

translations.literal: Presently Supervising Secretary Zheng Ya was commissioned to inspect Guizhou; he invited Shangyin as administrative aide of the observation commission and acting vice director of the Ministry of Waterways.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Supervising Secretary Zheng Ya was sent to inspect Guizhou. He invited Shangyin to serve as administrative aide on the observation staff and acting vice director of the Ministry of Waterways.

sentences.zh: 大中初，白敏中执政，令狐绹在内署，共排李德裕逐之。

translations.literal: In the early Dazhong era Bai Minzhong held power; Linghu Tao was in the inner secretariat; together they drove out Li Deyu.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dazhong reign Bai Minzhong came to power, with Linghu Tao in the inner secretariat; together they forced Li Deyu from office.

sentences.zh: 亚坐德裕党，亦贬循州刺史。

translations.literal: Ya was implicated as a member of Deyu's faction and was also demoted to prefect of Xunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ya was condemned as a member of Deyu's faction and was demoted to prefect of Xunzhou.

sentences.zh: 商隐随亚在岭表累载。

translations.literal: Shangyin followed Ya in the Lingnan region for several years.
translations.idiomatic: Shangyin followed Ya in the far south for several years.

sentences.zh: 三年入朝，京兆尹卢弘正奏署掾曹，令典笺奏。

translations.literal: After three years he entered court; the capital intendant Lu Hongzheng memorialized to appoint him to his staff and had him oversee petitions and memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he returned to court. The capital intendant Lu Hongzheng memorialized to place him on his staff and put him in charge of petitions and memorials.

sentences.zh: 明年，令狐绹作相，商隐屡启陈情，绹不之省。

translations.literal: The next year Linghu Tao became chief minister; Shangyin repeatedly submitted petitions explaining his situation, but Tao paid no attention.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Linghu Tao became chief minister. Shangyin repeatedly petitioned to explain his circumstances, but Tao ignored him.

sentences.zh: 弘正镇徐州，又从为掌书记。

translations.literal: When Hongzheng was commissioner at Xuzhou, Shangyin again followed him as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongzheng governed Xuzhou, Shangyin again served him as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 府罢入朝，复以文章干襜，乃补太学博士。

translations.literal: When the office expired he returned to court; he again sought advancement through his writings and was appointed Erudite of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: When that appointment ended he returned to court, again pressed his literary writings in search of office, and was appointed Erudite of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 会河南尹柳仲郢镇东蜀，辟为节度判官、检校工部郎中。

translations.literal: Presently the Henan intendant Liu Zhongying was commissioned to the eastern Shu region; he recruited Shangyin as military commissioner's administrative aide and acting director of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Henan intendant Liu Zhongying was sent to govern the eastern Shu region. He recruited Shangyin as administrative aide on his staff and acting director of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 大中末，仲郢坐专杀左迁，商隐废罢，还郑州，未几病卒。

translations.literal: In the late Dazhong period Zhongying was demoted for unauthorized execution; Shangyin was dismissed, returned to Zhengzhou, and soon after died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Dazhong reign Zhongying was demoted for an unauthorized execution. Shangyin was dismissed, returned to Zhengzhou, and died of illness not long afterward.

sentences.zh: 商隐能为古文，不喜偶对。

translations.literal: Shangyin could write in the ancient style and disliked parallel couplets.
translations.idiomatic: Shangyin could write in the ancient prose style and disliked regulated parallel composition.

sentences.zh: 从事令狐楚幕。

translations.literal: He served on Linghu Chu's staff.
translations.idiomatic: He had served on Linghu Chu's staff.

sentences.zh: 楚能章奏，遂以其道授商隐，自是始为今体章奏。

translations.literal: Chu was skilled at memorials and decrees and thus transmitted this art to Shangyin; from then on he began writing modern-style memorials and decrees.
translations.idiomatic: Chu excelled at memorials and edicts and taught Shangyin that craft, after which Shangyin began to write in the contemporary style of court documents.

sentences.zh: 博学强记，下笔不能自休，尤善为诔奠之辞。

translations.literal: Broad in learning and strong in memory, he could not stop once he set pen to paper, and was especially adept at dirges and offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Learned and with a formidable memory, he wrote tirelessly once he took up the brush and was especially skilled at dirges and funeral offerings.

sentences.zh: 与太原温庭筠、南郡段成式齐名，时号“三十六”。

translations.literal: He was famed alongside Wen Tingyun of Taiyuan and Duan Chengshi of Nancheng; at the time they were called the Thirty-six.
translations.idiomatic: His fame stood with Wen Tingyun of Taiyuan and Duan Chengshi of Nancheng; contemporaries called them the "Thirty-six."

sentences.zh: 文思清丽，庭筠过之。

translations.literal: His literary thought was clear and beautiful; he surpassed Tingyun.
translations.idiomatic: His literary sensibility was clear and refined, and in this he surpassed Tingyun.

sentences.zh: 而俱无持操，恃才诡激，为当涂者所薄。

translations.literal: Yet both lacked moral constancy; relying on talent they were eccentric and incendiary, and those in power despised them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet both lacked firm moral principle. They relied on talent, behaved with eccentric vehemence, and men in power looked down on them.

sentences.zh: 名宦不进，坎壈终身。

translations.literal: They did not advance in official fame and were frustrated throughout life.
translations.idiomatic: Neither advanced in official career and both were thwarted to the end of their lives.

sentences.zh: 弟羲叟，亦以进士擢第，累为宾佐。

translations.literal: His younger brother Yishou also passed the jinshi and served repeatedly as a staff member.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yishou also passed the jinshi examination and served repeatedly on provincial staffs.

sentences.zh: 商隐有表状集四十卷。

translations.literal: Shangyin had a collection of memorials and petitions in forty juan.
translations.idiomatic: Shangyin left a collection of memorials and formal petitions in forty juan.

sentences.zh: 吳通玄，海州人。

translations.literal: Wu Tongxuan was a man of Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Tongxuan came from Haizhou.

sentences.zh: 父道瓘為道士，善教誘童孺，大曆中，召入宮，為太子諸王授經。

translations.literal: His father Daojian was a Daoist priest skilled at instructing children; in the Dali era he was summoned to the palace to teach the crown prince and princes.
translations.idiomatic: His father Daojian was a Daoist priest skilled at teaching children. In the Dali reign he was summoned to court to instruct the crown prince and the imperial princes in the classics.

sentences.zh: 德宗在東宮，師道瓘，而通玄兄弟，出入宮掖，恆侍太子遊，故遇之厚。

translations.literal: When Dezong was crown prince he studied under Daojian; the Tongxuan brothers came and went within the inner palace and constantly attended the crown prince in his diversions, so they received generous favor.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong was still crown prince he studied under Daojian. The Tongxuan brothers moved freely within the inner palace and constantly attended the prince in his pastimes, and for this they won exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 通玄與兄通微，俱博學善屬文，文彩綺麗。

translations.literal: Tongxuan and his elder brother Tongwei were both erudite and skilled at composition; their literary coloring was ornate.
translations.idiomatic: Tongxuan and his elder brother Tongwei were both learned and skilled at literary composition, their style rich and ornate.

sentences.zh: 通玄幼應神童舉，釋褐祕書正字、左驍衞兵曹、大理評事。

translations.literal: Tongxuan in youth responded to the Child Prodigy examination; his first appointment was Regular Scribe in the Secretariat, clerk in the Left Courageous Guards, and reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Tongxuan passed the Child Prodigy examination. His first offices were Regular Scribe in the Secretariat, clerk in the Left Courageous Guards, and reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 建中初，策賢良方正等科，通玄應文詞清麗，登乙第，授同州司戶、京兆戶曹。

translations.literal: In the early Jianzhong period at the examination for worthies and the upright, Tongxuan responded in the category of elegant literary phrasing, placed in the second tier, and was appointed registrar of Tong prefecture and household registrar of the capital district.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianzhong reign, at the examination for worthies and upright men, Tongxuan entered the category for elegant literary phrasing, placed in the second tier, and was appointed registrar of Tong prefecture and household registrar of the capital district.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，召充翰林學士。

translations.literal: In the early Zhenyuan era he was summoned to serve as Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenyuan reign he was summoned to serve as a Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 遷起居舍人、知制誥，與陸贄、吉中孚、韋執誼等同視草。

translations.literal: He was promoted to diarist-attendant in attendance and drafter of edicts, and with Lu Zhi, Ji Zhongfu, Wei Zhiyi and others jointly drafted imperial documents.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to diarist-attendant and drafter of edicts, and together with Lu Zhi, Ji Zhongfu, Wei Zhiyi, and others shared the duty of drafting imperial documents.

sentences.zh: 陸贄富詞藻，特承德宗重顧，經歷艱難，通玄弟兄又以東宮侍上，由是爭寵，頗相嫌恨。

translations.literal: Lu Zhi was rich in diction and especially received Dezong's heavy regard because he had shared hard times; the Tongxuan brothers had also served the emperor when he was crown prince — hence they contended for favor and largely bore mutual resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi was richly gifted in language and enjoyed Dezong's special trust because he had shared the hardships of exile. The Tongxuan brothers had likewise attended the emperor when he was crown prince. The two sides therefore competed for favor and came to resent one another deeply.

sentences.zh: 贄性褊急，屢於上前短通玄，又言：「承平時工藝書畫之徒，待詔翰林，比無學士，只自至德後，天子召集賢學士于禁中草書詔，因在翰林院待進止，遂以為名。

translations.literal: Zhi was narrow and impatient by nature. He repeatedly criticized Tongxuan before the throne, and also said: "In peaceful times craftsmen, painters and calligraphers waited upon the throne in the Hanlin — formerly there were no 'academicians'; only from the Zhide era onward did the Son of Heaven gather worthy scholars in the palace to draft edicts in cursive script. Because they waited in the Hanlin Academy for orders, the title arose."
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was narrow and quick-tempered by nature. He repeatedly denounced Tongxuan before the throne and argued: "In peaceful times craftsmen, painters, and calligraphers merely waited on the emperor in the Hanlin. There were no 'academicians' as such. Only after the Zhide era did the Son of Heaven gather worthy scholars within the palace to draft edicts in draft script. Because they waited in the Hanlin Academy for orders, the title came into use."

sentences.zh: 奔播之時，道途或豫除改，權令草制。

translations.literal: In times of flight and turmoil, appointments might be made in advance on the road, and drafting was entrusted to them as a temporary measure.
translations.idiomatic: In times of flight and disorder appointments were sometimes made on the road in advance, and drafting was entrusted to them only as an expedient.

sentences.zh: 今四方無事，百揆時序，制書職分，宜歸中書舍人。

translations.literal: Now the four quarters are at peace and all ministries are in order; the division of labor for edicts should return to the drafters of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Now the realm is at peace and every ministry is in its proper course. The duty of drafting edicts should return to the Secretariat drafters.

sentences.zh: 學士之名，理須停寢。

translations.literal: The name "academician" should by rights be suspended.
translations.idiomatic: The title of Hanlin academician ought by rights to be abolished.

sentences.zh: 」贄以通玄援引朋黨，於禁中叶力排己，故欲廢之，德宗不許。

translations.literal: Zhi believed Tongxuan had brought in a clique of friends and within the palace actively worked to exclude him; therefore he wished to abolish the academy. Dezong did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi believed Tongxuan had brought in a faction of allies and was working within the palace to exclude him, and for that reason he wished to abolish the Hanlin Academy. Dezong would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 會贄權知兵部侍郎，知貢舉，乃正拜之，罷內職，皆通玄譖之也。

translations.literal: When Zhi was placed in charge of the Ministry of Personnel and conducted the civil service examinations, he was then formally appointed and his inner office duties were terminated — all owing to Tongxuan's slander.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhi was placed in charge of the Ministry of Personnel and conducted the civil service examinations, he received a formal appointment and was removed from inner-court duties — all because Tongxuan had slandered him.

sentences.zh: 七年，自起居郎拜諫議大夫、知制誥。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was promoted from diarist to Remonstrator and Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was promoted from diarist to Remonstrator and Drafter of Edicts.

sentences.zh: 通玄自以久次當拜中書舍人，而反除諫議，殊失望。

translations.literal: Tongxuan himself thought that after long seniority he should be appointed Secretariat Drafter, but was instead made Remonstrator and was deeply disappointed.
translations.idiomatic: Tongxuan had expected that after long seniority he would be appointed Secretariat Drafter, but was made Remonstrator instead and was deeply disappointed.

sentences.zh: 陸贄與宰相竇參相惡。

translations.literal: Lu Zhi and the chief minister Dou Can were mutually hostile.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi and the chief minister Dou Can were bitter enemies.

sentences.zh: 參從子給事中申，參尤寵之，每預中書擬議，所至人呼申為「喜鵲」。

translations.literal: Can's nephew by marriage, Attendant-in-waiting Shen, was especially favored by Can and took part in every Secretariat discussion; wherever he went people called Shen "the Magpie."
translations.idiomatic: Can's nephew by marriage, Attendant-in-waiting Shen, was especially favored by Can and took part in every Secretariat deliberation. Wherever he appeared people called him "the Magpie."

sentences.zh: 申，嗣虢王則之從父甥也。

translations.literal: Shen was a cousin on his father's side of Li Zezhi, who succeeded to the princedom of Guo.
translations.idiomatic: Shen was a paternal cousin of Li Zezhi, heir to the princedom of Guo.

sentences.zh: 申與則之親善。

translations.literal: Shen and Zezhi were on intimate terms.
translations.idiomatic: Shen and Zezhi were close friends.

sentences.zh: 則之為金吾將軍，好學有文，申與則之潛結吳通玄兄弟，為參共傾陸贄。

translations.literal: Zezhi was a general of the Imperial Guards, fond of study and skilled in letters; Shen and Zezhi secretly allied with the Wu Tongxuan brothers to overthrow Lu Zhi on Dou Can's behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Zezhi was a general of the Imperial Guards, fond of learning and skilled in letters. Shen and Zezhi secretly joined the Wu Tongxuan brothers in a plot to bring down Lu Zhi on Dou Can's behalf.

sentences.zh: 則之令人造謗書，言贄考試舉人不實，招納賄賂。

translations.literal: Zezhi had someone forge a defamatory document saying Zhi's examination of candidates was fraudulent and that he had accepted bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Zezhi had someone compose a libelous letter accusing Zhi of conducting the examinations dishonestly and accepting bribes.

sentences.zh: 時通玄取宗 室女為外婦，德宗知之。

translations.literal: At the time Tongxuan had taken an imperial clan woman as a concubine outside marriage; Dezong knew of it.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Tongxuan had taken an imperial clanswoman as an illicit consort, and Dezong already knew of it.

sentences.zh: 既聞申、則之譖陸贄，綱紀伺之，果與通玄結構其謀，帝大怒，罷竇參知政事，尋貶郴州司馬，竇申錦州司戶，李則之昭州司馬，通玄泉州司馬。

translations.literal: Having heard that Shen and Zezhi had slandered Lu Zhi, the authorities watched them and found they had indeed conspired with Tongxuan; the Emperor was furious, removed Dou Can from office, and soon demoted Can to secretary at Chen prefecture, Shen to registrar at Jin prefecture, Li Zezhi to secretary at Zhao prefecture, and Tongxuan to secretary at Quan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor learned that Shen and Zezhi had slandered Lu Zhi, investigators watched them and confirmed that they had plotted with Tongxuan. The emperor was enraged. He removed Dou Can from the chief ministership and soon demoted Can to secretary at Chen, Shen to registrar at Jin, Li Zezhi to secretary at Zhao, and Tongxuan to secretary at Quan.

sentences.zh: 帝召見之，親自臨 問，責以污辱近屬。

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned him for a personal audience and interrogated him, rebuking him for staining the honor of the imperial kin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Tongxuan for a personal audience, questioned him himself, and rebuked him for dishonoring the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 行至華州長城驛，賜死。

translations.literal: When he reached Great Wall Post on Huazhou circuit, he was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Great Wall Post in Huazhou, he was ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 尋以陸贄為中書侍郎、平章事，代竇參。

translations.literal: Soon Lu Zhi was made vice director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor in place of Dou Can.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Lu Zhi was appointed vice director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor in Dou Can's place.

sentences.zh: 通微，建中四年自壽安縣令入為金部員外，召充翰林學士。

translations.literal: Tongwei, in the fourth year of Jianzhong, entered from magistrate of Shou'an as outer court director in the Ministry of Revenue and was summoned as Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: Tongwei, in the fourth year of Jianzhong, rose from magistrate of Shou'an to outer-court director in the Ministry of Revenue and was then summoned as Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 尋改職方郎中，知制誥。

translations.literal: Shortly he was changed to director in the Ministry of Personnel and drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to director in the Ministry of Personnel and drafter of edicts.

sentences.zh: 與弟通玄同職禁署，人士榮之。

translations.literal: He held the same post in the forbidden secretariat as his younger brother Tongxuan; scholars regarded this as glorious.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the same forbidden secretariat as his younger brother Tongxuan, to the envy of the scholarly world.

sentences.zh: 七年，改禮部郎中，尋轉中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was changed to director in the Ministry of Rites, then transferred to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was made director in the Ministry of Rites and soon afterward promoted to Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 通玄死，素服待罪於國門，帝特宥之，通微竟不敢為喪服。

translations.literal: When Tongxuan died, Tongwei wore plain robes and awaited punishment at the national gate; the Emperor especially pardoned him, but Tongwei in the end did not dare wear mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When Tongxuan died, Tongwei appeared at the capital gate in plain robes to await punishment. The emperor specially pardoned him, yet Tongwei still did not dare observe mourning for his brother.

sentences.zh: 通玄詞藻婉麗，帝尤憐之。

translations.literal: Tongxuan's phrasing was graceful; the Emperor especially favored him.
translations.idiomatic: Tongxuan's diction was graceful and elegant, and the emperor favored him above all others.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，昭德王皇后崩，詔李紓為諡冊文，宰相張延賞、柳渾為廟樂章。

translations.literal: In the early Zhenyuan era Empress Zhao of virtue died; the decree ordered Li Shu to draft the posthumous title and eulogy, and the chief ministers Zhang Yanshang and Liu Hun the temple hymns.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenyuan reign Empress Zhaode died. The court ordered Li Shu to draft her posthumous title and eulogy, and the chief ministers Zhang Yanshang and Liu Hun to compose the temple hymns.

sentences.zh: 及進，皆不稱旨，並召通玄重撰。

translations.literal: When these were presented none pleased; all were summoned to have Tongxuan rewrite them.
translations.idiomatic: When the drafts were submitted none satisfied the throne, and Tongxuan alone was summoned to rewrite them.

sentences.zh: 凡中旨撰述，非通玄之筆，無不慊然，重之如此。

translations.literal: For every central drafting assignment, if it was not Tongxuan's brushwork the Emperor was never satisfied — such was the esteem in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: For every important drafting assignment from the throne, if the text was not Tongxuan's the emperor was never content — such was the regard in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 王仲舒字弘中，太原人。

translations.literal: Wang Zhongshu, style name Hongzhong, was a man of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhongshu, whose courtesy name was Hongzhong, came from Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 少孤貧，事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: Orphaned young and poor, he was known for filial devotion to his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned while young and poor, he became known for filial devotion to his mother.

sentences.zh: 嗜學工文，不就鄉舉。

translations.literal: Fond of study and skilled at letters, he would not take the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and excelled at letters, but refused to sit for the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 凡與結交，必知名之士，與楊頊、梁肅、裴樞為忘形之契。

translations.literal: Whomever he befriended had to be a man of reputation; with Yang Xian, Liang Su, and Pei Shu he formed bonds of complete intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: He would befriend only men of established reputation. With Yang Xian, Liang Su, and Pei Shu he formed friendships without reserve.

sentences.zh: 貞元十年，策試賢良方正能直言極諫等科，仲舒登乙第，超拜右拾遺。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Zhenyuan at the examination for worthies, upright men able to speak frankly and remonstrate fully, etc., Zhongshu placed in the second tier and was promoted directly to Right Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: In 794, at the examination for worthies and upright men able to speak frankly and remonstrate boldly, Zhongshu placed in the second tier and was promoted directly to Right Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 裴延齡領度支，矯誕大言，中傷良善，仲舒上疏極論之。

translations.literal: Pei Yanling headed the Revenue Commission; with inflated falsehoods and grand talk he harmed the virtuous; Zhongshu submitted a memorial arguing fully against him.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yanling headed the Revenue Commission. With boastful falsehoods he slandered the worthy, and Zhongshu submitted a memorial denouncing him at length.

sentences.zh: 累轉尚書郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to various director posts in the Six Ministries.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession through director posts in the central ministries.

sentences.zh: 元和五年，自職方郎中知制誥。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yuanhe he rose from director in the Ministry of Personnel to Drafter of Edicts.
translations.idiomatic: In 810 he advanced from director in the Ministry of Personnel to Drafter of Edicts.

sentences.zh: 仲舒文思溫雅，制誥所出，人皆傳寫。

translations.literal: Zhongshu's literary thought was warm and elegant; whatever edicts and decrees issued from him were copied by all.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshu wrote with a warm, elegant mind, and every edict that left his desk was copied and circulated.

sentences.zh: 京兆尹楊憑為中丞李夷簡所劾，貶臨賀尉。

translations.literal: The capital intendant Yang Ping was impeached by Senior Grand Secretary Li Yijian and was demoted to district defender of Linhe.
translations.idiomatic: The capital intendant Yang Ping was impeached by the censor-in-chief Li Yijian and demoted to district defender of Linhe.

sentences.zh: 仲舒與憑善，宣言於朝，言夷簡掎摭憑罪，仲舒坐貶硤州刺史。

translations.literal: Zhongshu was friendly with Ping and proclaimed at court that Yijian had framed Ping's crimes; Zhongshu was punished by demotion to prefect of Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshu was on friendly terms with Ping and declared openly at court that Yijian had manufactured charges against him. For this Zhongshu was demoted to prefect of Xia.

sentences.zh: 遷蘇州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，復召為中書舍人。

translations.literal: When Muzong took the throne, Zhongshu was again summoned as Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Muzong ascended the throne, Zhongshu was recalled and appointed Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 其年出為洪州刺史、御史中丞、江南西道觀察使。

translations.literal: That same year he went out as prefect of Hong, as chief of the imperial censors, and as observation commissioner of Jiangnan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he was sent out as prefect of Hong, imperial censor-in-chief, and observation commissioner of Jiangnan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 江西前例榷酒私釀法深，仲舒至鎮，奏罷之。

translations.literal: Jiangxi had by precedent heavy laws against the wine monopoly and private brewing; when Zhongshu reached his post he memorialized to abolish them.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi had long enforced harsh laws against private brewing under the wine monopoly. When Zhongshu took up his post he memorialized to repeal them.

sentences.zh: 又出官錢二萬貫，代貧戶輸稅。

translations.literal: He also disbursed twenty thousand strings of official cash to pay taxes on behalf of poor households.
translations.idiomatic: He also drew twenty thousand strings from official funds to pay taxes for impoverished households.

sentences.zh: 長慶三年冬，卒于鎮。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year of Changqing he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of 823 he died at his post.
